quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! Their wings beat in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second, allowing them to hover in place and even fly upside down for short distances. These tiny acrobats migrate thousands of miles each year despite weighing less than a nickel.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Tide Pools
short_read.teaser: Discover the colorful world that appears when the tide goes out along rocky shores. These miniature ocean worlds are full of surprising creatures right in your own backyard along the Strait.

medium_read.title: How Gardens Help Us Age Well
medium_read.teaser: Scientists are discovering what gardeners have always known — tending plants is good for body, mind, and spirit. From strengthening hands to lifting moods, gardens offer gentle medicine at every age.

long_read.title: The Danube: Europe's River of Many Stories
long_read.teaser: Journey along the legendary river that flows through ten countries, including Hungary. From Vienna's grand palaces to Budapest's thermal baths, the Danube has shaped European history, culture, and cuisine for thousands of years.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: July is a wonderful time to spot black-tailed deer grazing in the meadows at Hurricane Ridge. These gentle creatures are often seen with their fawns in the early morning or late afternoon, peacefully munching on wildflowers against the backdrop of snow-capped peaks. They're surprisingly comfortable around people and make for beautiful photo opportunities.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute when active.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You're right — 1,200 beats per minute! That tiny heart works incredibly hard to power such energetic flight.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute when they're active — that's 20 times every second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts are remarkably fast — beating about 1,200 times per minute! That's what it takes to power their incredible hovering and backwards flight.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: When a hummingbird is at rest, their heart rate slows to about 250 beats per minute. During sleep, they can enter a hibernation-like state called torpor where their heart rate drops to just 50 beats per minute to conserve energy.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Gyönyörű! That's right — pillangó means butterfly! Such a lovely, dancing word for such a lovely, dancing creature.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word is pillangó! Doesn't it sound like something fluttering? (Virág means flower, madár means bird, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungary is home to over 180 species of butterflies, including the beautiful swallowtails and the rare Large Blue. Hungarian meadows filled with wildflowers create perfect habitats for these delicate creatures.

puzzle_3.question: What color is a ruby-throated hummingbird's throat feathers?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! The male ruby-throated hummingbird has brilliant iridescent red throat feathers called a gorget. In certain light, it looks like he's wearing a glowing ruby necklace!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The answer is iridescent red! That's why they're called 'ruby-throated.' The males have these brilliant red throat feathers that shimmer like jewels in the sunlight. The females have white throats.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Ruby-throated hummingbirds are the most common hummingbird in eastern North America and the only species that regularly nests east of the Mississippi River. These tiny migrants fly 500 miles non-stop across the Gulf of Mexico twice a year!
